title: AddTenantCostRollup migration fails on TimescaleDB ≥2.18 — RLS after columnstore enable is rejected; blocks every deploy
evidence: log: aqua-db-migrate ... migration: AddTenantCostRollup1805000000000, error: operation not supported on hypertables that have columnstore enabled
rule_violated: TimescaleDB ≥2.18 reframes `timescaledb.compress` as columnstore mode on the hypertable; once columnstore is on, the engine rejects subsequent vanilla `ALTER TABLE ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`. Migrations that touch hypertable RLS must run RLS *before* the compression configuration, not after.
notes: Symptom: db-migrate container exits with `Migration failed ... operation not supported on hypertables that have columnstore enabled` BEFORE any service container starts; entire deploy chain blocks at this single migration. Architectural fix (T1, reorder operations to honour columnstore lock-out): up() now runs CREATE TABLE → CREATE INDEX → RLS (ENABLE/FORCE/CREATE POLICY) → create_hypertable → SET (timescaledb.compress, ...) → add_compression_policy → add_retention_policy. down() reordered to remove TimescaleDB policies first, then DROP TABLE CASCADE — avoids the columnstore-vs-ALTER restriction entirely (no intermediate ALTER TABLE / DROP POLICY needed; CASCADE tears down policies, RLS state, indexes, hypertable metadata, columnstore chunks in one shot). Sensor-service migration (sensor-service/src/database/migrations/1735900000000-CreateSensorMetrics.ts) audited and is unaffected — it has compression but no RLS, so no ordering conflict.

title: AddTenantCostRollup migration — TimescaleDB ≥2.18 enforces RLS ⊥ columnstore mutual exclusion; reorder alone insufficient
evidence: log: error: "columnstore cannot be used on table with row security"
rule_violated: TimescaleDB ≥2.18 enforces a HARD MUTUAL EXCLUSION between RLS and columnstore on the same hypertable. The RLS-first reorder under INFRA-CRITICAL-006 traded `operation not supported on hypertables that have columnstore enabled` (compression-then-RLS) for `columnstore cannot be used on table with row security` (RLS-then-compression). Engine refuses both sequences — order does not unlock either side.
notes:
Architectural fork (must pick ONE):
  (A) keep columnstore, drop RLS — moves tenant isolation enforcement entirely to the service layer.
  (B) keep RLS, drop columnstore — preserves DB-level defense-in-depth, loses ~50% storage savings on cold buckets.

Decision: (B). User-confirmed (response: 'b'). Rationale:
- Multi-tenant SaaS — tenant isolation is the load-bearing invariant; RLS is the DB-level guard.
- Table scale at documented retention: ~29k rows/day × 90 days = ~2.6M rows total; PostgreSQL handles this trivially.
- Compression savings (~1-2 GB/year) are immaterial vs the integrity guarantee.
- Future cold-storage compression can be reintroduced via a continuous aggregate (no RLS on the aggregate, RLS-equivalent filter pushed into the materialized query) when the dataset grows enough to justify it.

Fix landed:
- Removed `ALTER TABLE … SET (timescaledb.compress, …)` block.
- Removed `add_compression_policy(…, INTERVAL '14 days', …)` call.
- Kept `create_hypertable` (for chunking) + `add_retention_policy(…, INTERVAL '90 days', …)` (for time-based pruning).
- Kept full RLS (ENABLE + FORCE + tenant_scope policy + observability_service_admin bypass).
- Down(): removed `remove_compression_policy` call (nothing to remove).
- Inline load-bearing comment documents the constraint, the architectural fork, and the chosen branch with rationale, so any future engineer attempting to add columnstore back will see the trade-off.

title: Boot signal `migration_runner_applied` never fires after db-migrate centralization — pattern only matched cold-start hot path
evidence: Deploy log run 24636862240 (boot signal assertion: 23 signal(s) pending across 12 services for 12+ rounds, all healthy)
rule_violated: WS7 / ADR-016 Phase F deploy gate: every service in required-signals.yaml MUST emit each declared signal within its window. After db-migrate centralization, every service's migration runner sees 0 pending migrations on warm start and logs `No pending migrations on "<schema>"` — that text does NOT contain the substring `migration(s)` (with parens), so the signal never matches and the deploy gate rejects every deploy even though all containers are healthy and migrations have been applied centrally.
notes:
Architectural fix (T1, single canonical signal source):

1. MigrationRunnerService.onApplicationBootstrap() now emits a canonical end-of-run log line — `Migration runner complete for schema "<sourceSchema>": tenants=<N>` — at the success exit. Fires unconditionally on both cold-start (>0 pending applied) and warm-start (0 pending) paths. Failure paths (security throw, runner exception) intentionally do NOT emit it, so the contract still proves the runner reached the success exit (no false positive).
2. required-signals.yaml signal_library.migration_runner_applied pattern updated from `"migration(s)"` (substring of "Applied N migration(s): …") to `"Migration runner complete"` (substring of the new canonical line).
3. The pre-existing per-schema logs (`Applied N migration(s) on "X"` and `No pending migrations on "X"`) are unchanged — they still document per-schema progress; they're just no longer the contract surface for the deploy gate.
4. Refactored the orphan `if (!tenantAware) return;` early-return into a single tenantAware branch so the canonical complete log lands once per runner invocation regardless of fan-out shape.

Why not change the signal pattern alone: a looser substring like `"migration"` would match `migration failed`, `running migration`, etc. — any noise word that happens to mention migrations would falsely satisfy the contract. The canonical-log approach pins the signal to a single emission point in the code, which is the discipline required by required-signals.yaml's signalSource convention.

title: pgvector extension absent from TimescaleDB postgres image — HNSW migration crashes on every fresh DB
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24637240275 log: operator class vector_cosine_ops does not exist for access method hnsw
rule_violated: Migration runs CREATE INDEX ... USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops) which requires pgvector ≥ 0.5.0. Stock TimescaleDB images do not include pgvector. Production is dormant-broken (warm-state DB, never re-runs migration); CI fresh DB triggers it on every run.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, single source of truth image): build infrastructure/docker/postgres/Dockerfile = FROM timescale/timescaledb:2.25.1-pg16 + apt-get install postgresql-16-pgvector. Publish to GHCR via .github/workflows/build-postgres-image.yml; reference the GHCR tag in e2e-messaging.yml + all 4 docker-compose.*.yml (droplet, dev, infra, prod). Add tests/invariants/postgres-image-uniformity.spec.ts that greps every yml and asserts only one image tag is used.

title: Schema drift — 11 entity↔DB violations on messaging-service
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24637240275 log: SchemaDriftValidator[messaging] schema.drift.detected — 11 violation(s)
rule_violated: ADR-012 schema-drift invariant: every @Column declaration must match the live DB column. After Root-A (synchronize removal) is fixed, the drift validator gives canonical readout. 4 NOT-NULL drifts + 7 missing columns require a single remediation migration that aligns DB to entity contracts.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, single remediation migration): apps/messaging-service/src/migrations/1782600000000-AlignMessagingEntityDrift.ts — Block 1: 7 ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS for missing columns. Block 2: assertNoNulls + UPDATE backfill + ALTER COLUMN SET NOT NULL for the 4 nullability convergence targets (mirrors 1782300000000 pattern). down(): symmetrical DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS + DROP NOT NULL. Tenant-aware schemas inherit via existing tenant-clone scaffolding (LIKE source INCLUDING ALL).

title: Test fixture creates partitions out-of-band with naming that collides with PartitionManagerService
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24637240275 log: partition messages_2026_04 would overlap partition messages_y2026m04
rule_violated: Two competing partition creators violate single-source-of-truth. Test fixture creates messages_y2026m04 BEFORE app starts; runtime PartitionManagerService.onApplicationBootstrap creates messages_2026_04 covering the same date range. PostgreSQL detects overlapping FOR VALUES (regardless of partition NAME) and rejects the second attempt — bricks every test that needs to write to messages or message_receipts in tenant schema.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, eliminate the duplicate creator): delete the partition creation block in e2e-setup.ts:380-430. PartitionManagerService.onApplicationBootstrap is the canonical SSoT (already runs at app bootstrap, ensures current + 2 future months). Add tests/invariants/single-partition-creator.spec.ts that greps for any non-runtime CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF outside migrations/ and partition-manager.service.ts and asserts zero hits.

title: GraphQL enum input coercion drops value-mapping → uppercase 'MEMBER' written to DB violates chk_member_role
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24637240275 log: new row for relation channel_members violates check constraint chk_member_role; failing row contains ... MEMBER, all, ...
rule_violated: TypeScript enum ChannelMemberRole has key MEMBER mapped to value 'member'. registerEnumType(ChannelMemberRole, { name: 'ChannelMemberRole' }) without explicit valuesMap leaks the enum NAME ('MEMBER') through to resolver param → command → handler → SQL. CHECK constraint allows lowercase only ('owner','admin','member'). Per OWASP input-boundary discipline, enum coercion must be the canonical normalization point.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, canonical input boundary normalization): replace bare registerEnumType with explicit valuesMap so GraphQL→TypeScript coercion writes the TypeScript enum VALUE, not the NAME. If valuesMap alone insufficient (NestJS GraphQL edge case for value-mapped string enums), add @Transform on AddChannelMemberInput DTO that maps GraphQL name to enum value. Apply same pattern to NotificationPreference. Add apps/messaging-service/src/channel/__tests__/role-enum-coercion.spec.ts as contract test.

title: Runtime dataSource.synchronize() in SourceSchemaBootstrapService creates wrong-shape columns + crashes on partitioned-table FK
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24637240275 deploy log: SourceSchemaBootstrapService Failed to bootstrap source schema ... there is no unique constraint matching given keys for referenced table messages
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md forbids dataSource.synchronize() in runtime: migrations are SSoT. NestJS onModuleInit fires BEFORE onApplicationBootstrap, so SourceSchemaBootstrapService runs synchronize before MessagingMigrationRunnerService. TypeORM 0.3.x cannot generate composite FK to partitioned messages(id, createdAt). Same synchronize call also creates columns with wrong nullability — silently corrupts every fresh DB.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, eliminate the contaminant): remove both synchronize() calls; move lifecycle hook from onModuleInit to onApplicationBootstrap with provider ordering after MessagingMigrationRunnerService; replace empty-schema branch with hard-fail message instructing operator to run db-migrate. Add tests/invariants/no-runtime-synchronize.spec.ts that greps the entire repo and asserts zero synchronize() callsites outside test setup files.

title: message_attachments.is_deleted partial index pending — needs CONCURRENTLY migration
rule_violated: Entity declares @Index() on is_deleted as a performance optimization for non-deleted-attachment lookups. The drift remediation migration could not include CREATE INDEX because R3 (migration-sql-lint) requires CONCURRENTLY for indexes on populated tables, and CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transactional migration.
notes: Follow-up: write a sibling migration with transactional=false that runs `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_attachments_is_deleted ON message_attachments (is_deleted) WHERE is_deleted = false`. Tenant-aware fan-out applies (one CONCURRENT index per source + per tenant schema). Performance-only optimization; not a correctness invariant; drift validator does NOT flag missing indexes so this does not re-open the deploy gate.

title: Illegal `value:` field in registerEnumType valuesMap blocks tsc — 12/12 messaging E2E + CI Affected backend build fail
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24638245324 (E2E messaging) job 72037454378 — 12/12 suites failed to compile, 0 tests run
GitHub Actions run 24638245327 (CI Affected) job 72037594216 — backend build failed with 12 TS2353 errors
rule_violated: NestJS EnumMetadataValuesMapOptions only accepts description? + deprecationReason?. The `value` field does not exist in the type signature. tsc --strict rejects unknown properties in mapped type literals. NestJS controls enum value coercion via the enum's own Object.entries(enum) — valuesMap is metadata-only.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, delete the dead-and-illegal field): remove the `, value: <Enum>.<KEY>` from each of the 6 valuesMap entries. Keep description-only. The actual GraphQL-name → TS-value boundary normalization lives in channel.resolver.ts:227 via `(ChannelMemberRole as Record<string, ChannelMemberRole>)[role] ?? role`. That's the canonical T1 coercion fix; the valuesMap was a misunderstood secondary attempt. No functional regression — runtime behaviour was already correct via the resolver normalization, the illegal field just blocked compilation.

title: required-signals.yaml expects per-service migration_runner_applied that 4 services structurally cannot emit
evidence: apps/auth-service/src/app.module.ts (uses TypeORM native migrationsRun:true, no createMigrationRunnerService)
apps/sensor-service/src/app.module.ts (passes migration classes via factory but TypeORM runs them natively)
GitHub Actions run 24637240276 deploy job 72035207338: 4 services missing 'Migration runner complete'
rule_violated: Per ADR-016 Phase E intent, aqua-db-migrate is the centralized SSoT for migration application. Per-service runners are Phase 1 backward-compat. The manifest expected per-service signals from runners that may or may not exist — contradicts SSoT and blocks deploy gates indefinitely.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, manifest realigned to SSoT): add db_migrate_complete signal_library entry pointing to apps/db-migrate/src/main.ts (already emits 'aqua-db-migrate complete' at line 246). Add aqua-db-migrate as services entry. Remove migration_runner_applied from per-service blocks. Per-service runners continue emitting as defense-in-depth. Add tests/invariants/required-signals-vs-emitters.spec.ts to lock manifest↔source contract.

title: observability-service does not register SchemaDriftModule — manifest signal cannot fire
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24637240276 deploy job 72035207338: observability-service missing 'Schema drift scan clean'
rule_violated: Per ADR-012 + the required-signals.yaml manifest, every service expected to emit schema_drift_clean MUST register SchemaDriftModule. Observability has the expectation but not the registration.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, register the module): observability has no @Entity() declarations, so validator runs against empty entityMetadatas and emits 'Schema drift scan clean: checked 0 entities' — substring matches the manifest pattern.

title: postgres-ssl-entrypoint.sh hardcoded uid 999 broke deploy after pgvector image swap (Ubuntu uid=1000)
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24653206569 deploy job 72081278019: 'Container aqua-postgres Error dependency postgres failed to start; container is unhealthy'
docker-compose.droplet.yml:162 image timescale/timescaledb-ha:pg16 (HA edition, Ubuntu base, postgres uid=1000)
Earlier image timescale/timescaledb:2.25.1-pg16 (Alpine base, postgres uid=999)
rule_violated: Image-family-coupled hardcoding violates the 'works with any postgres image' contract that container entrypoints should honor. The pgvector image swap (commit b11bac15) silently broke production cert ownership because the entrypoint script assumed Alpine uid conventions.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, image-agnostic uid resolution): replace hardcoded `chown 999:999` with `chown $(id -u postgres):$(id -g postgres)`. Falls back to 999 only if the user doesn't exist. Works on Alpine (uid 999), Debian/Ubuntu (uid 1000), and any future image with a `postgres` user. The certs now get the correct ownership regardless of which postgres image the compose file references. Production deploy chain unblocked once this lands and the droplet pulls the updated entrypoint script.

title: HA postgres image default PGDATA path differs from legacy image — initdb fails on existing volume
evidence: Live droplet log: 'initdb: error: directory /home/postgres/pgdata/data exists but is not empty'
rule_violated: Image-family-specific PGDATA defaults break compose volume reuse. The pgvector image swap (b11bac15) silently changed the postgres data directory expectation; the existing volume mount points at the legacy path; HA image's initdb tries to bootstrap a different (image-baked, mostly-empty) directory and fails because it's not empty.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, explicit PGDATA pin across all compose files): set PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data env var explicitly in docker-compose.{droplet,prod,dev,infra,base}.yml so the HA image uses the same data path as the legacy image. Single source of truth across every environment. Combined with INFRA-CRITICAL-017 (dynamic uid resolution) + the one-shot volume chown (70 → 1000) on the droplet, postgres now boots cleanly from existing data using the new HA image.

title: MODULE_SCHEMAS lists orphan tables (supplier_sites, site_contacts) — SourceSchemaBootstrapService crashes farm-service
evidence: apps/farm-service/src/supplier/entities/supplier-site.entity.ts:7-10 ('Orphan entity - not registered in any module forFeature')
Live droplet logs: 'Source schema farm is missing 2/69 declared tables: supplier_sites, site_contacts'
rule_violated: Per ADR-011, MODULE_SCHEMAS lists ACTIVE tables only. Orphan @Entity() declarations are entity-side tech debt, not schema ownership claims. Listing them crashed SourceSchemaBootstrapService after INFRA-CRITICAL-009 made missing-table verification hard-fail.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, MODULE_SCHEMAS reflects active tables only): remove supplier_sites + site_contacts from farm MODULE_SCHEMAS.tables. Inline comment documents the orphan status. When architectural decision to USE these entities is taken, write migration AND re-add to MODULE_SCHEMAS in SAME commit.

title: Messaging E2E race: SourceSchemaBootstrapService.onApplicationBootstrap fires BEFORE MessagingMigrationRunnerService
evidence: GitHub Actions run 24655383286 messaging E2E job 72087509759: 'Source schema messaging is empty AFTER application bootstrap... Refusing to fall back to runtime synchronize() per INFRA-CRITICAL-009'
12/12 test suites failed at bootstrap stage; 0 tests ran
rule_violated: Both SourceSchemaBootstrapService and MessagingMigrationRunnerService register onApplicationBootstrap. NestJS calls them in declaration order; SourceSchemaBootstrapService fires FIRST and finds an empty source schema (migrations haven't run yet). My INFRA-CRITICAL-009 hard-fail then kills the bootstrap. Production is unaffected (aqua-db-migrate runs before service container starts, per compose dependency chain) but E2E tests boot the AppModule directly and have no such pre-stage.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, env-aware migration timing): add migrationsRunFromEnv to messaging-service's createServiceTypeOrmConfig call. Test (DATABASE_MIGRATIONS_RUN=true) → TypeORM runs migrations at DataSource init, BEFORE any NestJS lifecycle hook fires → SourceBootstrap finds tables → no false-fail. Production (DATABASE_MIGRATIONS_RUN=false) → unchanged, aqua-db-migrate runs first via compose. The MessagingMigrationRunnerService becomes a verify-only no-op in both paths but stays as defense-in-depth.

title: Cross-service entity contamination via @aquaculture/backend-common main barrel — every service auto-loads AuditLogEntity/UserConsent/GdprDataRequest/FindingEntity, surfacing as ~30 cross-schema drift violations per service
evidence: Live droplet drift output 2026-04-20: farm-service=89 violations, admin-api=132, billing=33, sensor=35, alert=30, auth=40, hr=24, notification=25, config=25, observability=3, hydroponics=1 — 30+ are cross-schema entity contamination
libs/backend-common/src/index.ts had `export * from './audit'` + `export * from './finding-registry'` triggering @Entity decorator side-effects on every consumer
libs/backend-common/src/security/index.ts had `export * from './gdpr'` triggering UserConsent + GdprDataRequest decorators

libs/backend-common/src/guards/tenant.guard.ts imported AuditLogService directly, chaining through audit-log.entity.ts → @Entity decorator runs in every service that uses TenantGuard (which is every service)
rule_violated: ADR-011 schema ownership: each entity belongs to exactly one service's schema. The transitive import-time @Entity decorator side-effect via the shared backend-common barrel made every service co-own foreign entities, breaking the SchemaDriftValidator's per-service ownership contract.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, dependency-inversion + barrel surgery): (1) New audit-log.tokens.ts file owns AUDIT_LOG_SERVICE Symbol token + IAuditLogService interface + AuditSeverity enum — NO @Entity import. (2) tenant.guard.ts depends on token+interface (not concrete AuditLogService class). (3) audit-log.module.ts provides AUDIT_LOG_SERVICE token alongside concrete class so existing concrete-class consumers stay green. (4) backend-common/src/index.ts no longer re-exports `./audit` or `./finding-registry`; security/index.ts no longer re-exports `./gdpr` — these are deep-import only via tsconfig path aliases @aquaculture/backend-common/{audit,gdpr,finding-registry}. (5) 10 consumer files mechanically rewritten to use the deep paths. (6) Invariant test tests/invariants/no-shared-entity-decorators-via-main-barrel.spec.ts locks the contract.

title: DEFECT-2: ~213 @Entity() decorators across 11 services declared no schema option, defaulting to 'public' and tripping the SchemaDriftValidator on every cold start
evidence: Live droplet drift output 2026-04-20: farm=89 violations, admin-api=132, billing=33, sensor=35, alert=30, auth=40, hr=24, notification=25, config=25, observability=3, hydroponics=1 — ~400 of these reduce to the missing schema option
Sample violation per service: '[farms] entity declares schema=public but table lives in farm', '[invoices] entity declares schema=public but table lives in billing', etc.
ADR-011 + CLAUDE.md Inviolable rule #2: Every @Entity() includes the schema: option. The mechanical convention had drifted across ~213 entity files.
rule_violated: ADR-011 schema ownership: every @Entity() must declare its schema explicitly so the SchemaDriftValidator can verify entity↔table alignment without false positives from the TypeORM 'schema=public' default.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, mechanical sweep + invariant): added { schema: '<svc>' } to 213 @Entity decorator calls across 185 files in 11 services (admin-api, auth, billing, config, event-store, farm, alert-engine, ai, hydroponics, sensor, plus a few in observability). Codemod handled three @Entity argument shapes: (1) @Entity('table') → adds 2nd arg, (2) @Entity('table', { ...opts }) → merges schema into opts, (3) @Entity({ name: 'table', ...opts }) → merges schema into opts. New invariant tests/invariants/entity-schema-declaration.spec.ts walks every apps/*/src/**/*.entity.ts and asserts every non-empty @Entity call carries a schema: option — locks the contract.

title: Phase D: env-aware migrationsRun was missing from 8 services that use MigrationRunnerService — every E2E test of those services would crash on SourceSchemaBootstrapService just like INFRA-CRITICAL-020 messaging E2E did
evidence: INFRA-CRITICAL-020 (commit 074c7807) added migrationsRunFromEnv to messaging-service to unblock E2E. The same race exists for every other service that uses MigrationRunnerService — when an E2E harness boots the AppModule against a fresh DB, SourceSchemaBootstrapService.onApplicationBootstrap fires before any migration runner could populate the schema, hard-failing per INFRA-CRITICAL-009.

8 services lacked migrationsRunFromEnv: farm, hr, alert-engine, billing, notification, config, hydroponics, ai. Discovered via `grep -L migrationsRunFromEnv apps/*-service/src/app.module.ts apps/alert-engine/src/app.module.ts`

messaging-service had it (074c7807); sensor-service had it (different default); admin-api/event-store had it (legacy 'true' default); auth uses `migrationsRun: true`; observability has `migrations: []`
rule_violated: Service migration-timing contract (INFRA-CRITICAL-020): every service that owns a source schema AND uses MigrationRunnerService must opt into the env-aware TypeORM runner so test harnesses can apply migrations before NestJS lifecycle hooks fire.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, mechanical sweep): added the env-aware migrationsRunFromEnv block to 8 services' createServiceTypeOrmConfig calls. Default 'false' = production-safe (aqua-db-migrate runs first in prod). E2E harnesses set DATABASE_MIGRATIONS_RUN=true to enable TypeORM's built-in runner at DataSource init. New invariant tests/invariants/all-services-env-aware-migrations.spec.ts asserts every service has the contract (or one of three documented alternatives: legacy 'true' default for admin-api/event-store, static migrationsRun:true for auth, migrations:[] for observability).

title: DEFECT-3: messaging E2E test harness lacked withTenantContext helper — direct dataSource.* calls in tests bypass the middleware-set ALS, causing TENANT_ISOLATION_VIOLATION on every direct write
evidence: GitHub Actions runs 24659776761 / 24660420932 / 24659561676 — every messaging E2E run shows hundreds of `TENANT_ISOLATION_VIOLATION: Direct write to source schema messaging.channels blocked`

Tenant routing is ALS-driven: requestContextStorage carries `schemaName = tenant_<uuid>`, the patched pg pool reads it on every checkout and pins search_path. Direct dataSource.* calls in tests run OUTSIDE any request → ALS empty → pool falls back to source schema → trigger fires.

apps/messaging-service/test/e2e-setup.ts (PRE-FIX): no helper to wrap direct DB calls in a synthetic ALS frame; tests had no clean way to perform fixture writes / OUTBOX inspection without tripping the source-schema write guard.
rule_violated: Test-environment tenant routing parity: anything that writes to a tenant-scoped table MUST run inside a tenant-scoped ALS frame so the patched pool routes the connection to the tenant schema. The production middleware chain establishes that frame for HTTP requests; tests doing direct DB calls need an explicit helper.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, parity-by-construction): added `withTenantContext(tenantId, fn)` helper to apps/messaging-service/test/e2e-setup.ts. Imports `requestContextStorage` from backend-common (the singleton ALS instance the production middleware + TenantConnectionBootstrap pool patch use), composes parent store + new store with `tenantId` + `schemaName = tenant_<uuid>`, runs `fn` inside the synthetic frame. Direct test-side dataSource calls now route to the tenant schema just like production GraphQL writes. Invariant tests/invariants/messaging-e2e-tenant-context.spec.ts asserts the helper exists, imports the right ALS instance, and composes the parent store (catches future regressions that would silently break tenant routing in tests). NOTE: this commit lands the helper; the residual `TENANT_ISOLATION_VIOLATION` errors observed in the GraphQL request flow on the same E2E runs have a separate root cause (ALS frame not propagating across some async boundary inside the NestJS CQRS / Apollo handler chain) and require a separate diagnostic + fix — tracked as the next finding.

title: Shared cross-tenant tables (audit_logs, user_consents, gdpr_data_requests) live in `admin` schema instead of canonical `shared` — every backend boot reports drift, blocks deploy boot-signal contract
evidence: Live droplet 2026-04-20 11:40: auth-service=2 drift violations [audit_logs/user_consents both 'declares schema=shared but lives in admin'], plus identical drift on alert-engine/billing-service/notification-service/config-service

ADR-011 + CLAUDE.md 'Tenant row placement (D14)': shared schema reserved for the 4 canonical cross-tenant tables (audit_logs, gdpr_data_requests, user_consents, user_permissions). user_permissions already in shared; the other 3 had drifted to admin.

Entity decorators in libs/backend-common/src/{audit,security/gdpr}/entities/*.entity.ts always declare { schema: 'shared' } — the divergence is in the DB, not the code. Boot-signal contract `schema_drift_clean` cannot fire while the divergence persists; deploy gate then triggers rollback.
rule_violated: ADR-011 schema ownership: the `shared` schema is the single source of truth for cross-tenant singletons. Tables physically placed elsewhere violate the ownership contract and surface as drift on every service that imports the relevant module.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, ALTER TABLE SET SCHEMA — atomic catalog move, no data copy): apps/admin-api-service/src/migrations/1782200000000-MoveSharedTablesFromAdminToShared.ts moves audit_logs/user_consents/gdpr_data_requests from admin to shared schema (creates shared schema if absent). Sequence ownership follow-up moves the SERIAL/BIGSERIAL sequences too. Idempotent — safe to re-run on already-migrated databases via IF EXISTS / IN-shared check. Migration registered in admin-api-service's app.module.ts migrations array; aqua-db-migrate centralized runner picks it up at next deploy. Closes the boot-signal `schema_drift_clean` gap on 5 services (auth/alert/billing/notification/config) — each had this drift as their sole or primary remaining violation. Other categories (hr-service 453 column violations, farm-service farm_outbox column gap, billing soft-delete columns, alert/billing tenant_id type drift, admin-api cross-schema entity refs) are separate findings tracked individually.

title: rumqttc 0.25.1 transitively pulls vulnerable rustls-webpki 0.102.8 (RUSTSEC-2026-0098 + 0099)
evidence: deny.toml [advisories] ignore = ["RUSTSEC-2026-0098", "RUSTSEC-2026-0099"] with full inline justification
rule_violated: deny.toml advisories check (vulnerable transitive dep)
notes: Resolution paths in priority order: (1) wait for rumqttc upstream to bump rustls-webpki to 0.103.12+ and cut a release; (2) fork rumqttc to crates/local-rumqttc with the dep bump and switch to a path dep; (3) replace rumqttc with mqtt-async-client / paho-mqtt-rs, which would also let us drop the deny.toml ignore. Threat model justification (low real-world risk): the CVEs allow a misissued cert with permitted-subtree wildcard name constraints to validate; our MQTT TLS chain trusts the platform's internal PKI (we issue every cert), not a public CA. An attacker would have to compromise the platform CA to mint such a cert. The ignore is therefore conservative — the impact is upstream library hygiene, not a reachable platform vulnerability.

title: farm.farm_outbox missing 5 modern OutboxEntityBase columns (tenantId, aggregateId, nextAttemptAt, idempotencyKey, isDeadLettered) — blocks SchemaDriftValidator boot signal
evidence: Live droplet 2026-04-20 11:40: farm-service drift validator reports 5 violations on every boot — `[farm.farm_outbox.<column>] entity declares column but DB has no such column`

platform/libs/outbox/src/outbox-entity.base.ts: OutboxEntityBase declares the 5 columns. Migration 1780300000000-CreateFarmOutboxTable.ts created the table BEFORE these columns existed in the base class. No follow-up migration ever added them.

FarmOutbox entity uses `synchronize: false` (correct), so TypeORM doesn't auto-add the columns — runtime publisher (platform/libs/outbox/src/outbox-publisher.service.ts) silently masks the gap by reading payload.tenantId from the JSONB blob instead of the column. Drift only visible since SchemaDriftValidator was wired into farm-service in Phase 11.4.
rule_violated: ADR-012 schema-drift-prevention: every entity column must have a matching DB column. The 5-column gap means the publisher's modern code paths (per-tenant subject routing, exponential-backoff polling, dedup index, fast dead-letter filter) are silently degraded — the JSONB-payload fallback works but loses the index-scannability of the column-based predicate.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, forward-only ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN — metadata-only operation in PG 11+ thanks to non-volatile DEFAULTs): apps/farm-service/src/database/migrations/1786200000000-AddFarmOutboxModernColumns.ts adds the 5 columns IF NOT EXISTS. Idempotent. Indexes (dedup unique + modern polling predicate) intentionally deferred to a follow-up CONCURRENTLY migration — CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY would take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on a pre-existing table. Migration registered in apps/farm-service/src/app.module.ts; aqua-db-migrate centralized runner picks it up via glob pattern. Closes farm-service's drift validator violation count from 5 to 0; unblocks `schema_drift_clean` boot signal for farm-service deploy gate.

title: billing.{subscriptions,invoices,payments} + alert.{alert_incidents,alert_audit_log} tenant_id is varchar in DB but entity declares uuid — RLS-incompatible drift, blocks deploy boot signal
evidence: Live droplet 2026-04-20 11:40 UTC: SchemaDriftValidator[billing] reports 7+ violations (3 tenant_id varchar/uuid + 6 missing soft-delete columns); SchemaDriftValidator[alert] reports 2 tenant_id varchar/uuid drifts on alert_incidents and alert_audit_log

title: SchemaDriftValidator validates synchronize:false read-view entities — emits 67 false positives on admin-api's billing.* cross-schema reads
evidence: Live droplet 2026-04-20 13:53 UTC: admin-api-service emits 68 violations: 1 real (admin.audit_logs table missing) + 67 false positives on billing.invoices/billing.subscriptions/billing.usage_aggregations/billing.tenant_usage_metrics. All 67 false-positive entities declare `synchronize: false` (TypeORM's marker for 'this is a read-view of another service's table; do not generate DDL').

Same root cause as INFRA-CRITICAL-034 permission-shadow (admin_service role can't enumerate billing.* columns via information_schema), but the architecturally correct fix differs: granting admin cross-schema SELECT would VIOLATE ADR-011 entity ownership (admin owns admin schema only; cross-schema reads should not be modeled as entities). Skipping synchronize:false entities in the validator preserves ADR-011 AND eliminates the false positives.

libs/backend-common/src/database/schema-drift-validator.service.ts (pre-Phase-J) — onApplicationBootstrap() iterates dataSource.entityMetadatas without checking entity.synchronize. TypeORM's own RdbmsSchemaBuilder skips synchronize-false entities for DDL generation; the drift validator did NOT mirror that semantics.

Each billing entity in apps/billing-service has its own SchemaDriftValidator that catches OWNER-side drift on billing.invoices/billing.subscriptions/etc. The admin-api consumer's read-view validation is therefore redundant — and incorrectly generates noise.
rule_violated: Architectural-coherence rule: validator semantics must mirror entity-ownership semantics. `synchronize: false` is TypeORM's canonical 'I do not own this table' marker. The drift validator must respect that marker — drift on a not-owned entity is the OWNER service's responsibility (and is caught by the OWNER's own SchemaDriftValidator instance per ADR-012). Validating not-owned entities double-reports drift AND emits false positives on the consumer side (consumer role typically lacks information_schema visibility on the foreign table).
notes: Architectural fix (T1, validator-semantics correction): two coordinated changes. (1) libs/backend-common/src/database/schema-drift-validator.service.ts — added per-entity check `if (entity.synchronize === false) { skippedNotOwned++; continue; }` before validateEntity(). Logs the skipped count alongside checked count: 'Schema drift scan clean: checked N owned entities, skipped M cross-schema read views (synchronize=false)'. (2) apps/admin-api-service/src/migrations/1787100000000-CreateAdminAuditLogsTable.ts — closes the 1 REAL drift in admin-api's 68 violations (admin.audit_logs table missing). CREATE TABLE matches apps/admin-api-service/src/audit/audit.entity.ts column shape 1:1 (16 columns + 6 indexes + audit_logs_severity_enum type). Indexes co-emitted with CREATE TABLE in single SQL chunk so migration-sql lint R3 recognizes them as 'index-on-new-table' (table empty at index-creation, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE safe). Idempotent (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS + CREATE TYPE wrapped in DO/EXCEPTION duplicate_object). Closes admin-api drift signal completely. Also supersedes INFRA-CRITICAL-032's follow-up plan to refactor admin-api's cross-schema entities to raw SQL — the synchronize:false marker is the canonical ADR-011-compliant signal AND the validator now respects it. The 5 consumer service files (analytics.service.ts, reports.service.ts, invoice-management.service.ts, support/messaging.service.ts, usage-metering-management.service.ts) remain using their TypeORM repositories — that's a legitimate read-only view pattern, not an antipattern, as long as the entities declare synchronize:false (which they all already do).

title: Task checklist items had no stable id and wrote `completed` vs `isCompleted` divergently — toggle was silently broken
rule_violated: Entity state consistency: every JSONB item with a client-targetable lookup key must have a server-assigned stable id, and every canonical boolean field must have a single source of truth across create / update / toggle write paths.
notes: Closed by this commit. Discovered during FARM-HIGH-001 type-safety follow-up. The TaskChecklistItemInput DTO had `text` + `isCompleted?` but no `id`, so created items had no stable key — every subsequent `toggleChecklistItem(itemId)` call ran `.find((i) => i.id === itemId)` against items with undefined ids and silently failed. The toggle also wrote `item.completed = !item.completed` while the input DTO wrote `isCompleted` — a UI reading `isCompleted` after toggle would see no change because the toggle wrote to a different field. title: Spec files in script-mode (no top-level import/export) silently leak top-level declarations into the global scope, masking strict-tsc collision errors
rule_violated: TypeScript spec files MUST be modules (carry at least one top-level import or export). Script-mode files leak top-level declarations into the global scope, allowing same-named declarations across files to collide. The collision is invisible to eslint and the test runner; only strict-tsc surfaces it, often with cascading 'unrelated' errors. Surfaced by PR #180 (libs/backend-common, observations §31).
notes: Closed by PR-37 (chore/spec-module-mode-invariant-pr37). Added tests/invariants/spec-module-mode.spec.ts that walks every *.spec.ts under apps/, libs/, platform/, tests/, web/ and asserts each carries at least one top-level import or export statement. 6 violators surfaced by the new invariant — all closed by adding `export {};` after the JSDoc header (one line per file). The bug pattern that motivated this invariant: PR-29 found that gha-sha-pin-gate.spec.ts and npm-audit-gate.spec.ts both declared `const runCheck = require(...)` at the top in script mode, the names collided in the global scope, and cross-file type-checking merged the wrong signature so npm-audit's runCheck(report,args) was strict-checked against gha-sha-pin's runCheck(): Array signature — 5 cascading errors that collapsed to 0 from one fix. Without this invariant, the same trap can recur whenever a new spec uses require() without import/export.

title: UserNotificationPreferences.channelConfigs over-strict: Record<NotificationChannel, ChannelConfig> requires all 7 channels even though production code reads via optional chain
rule_violated: Type declarations should reflect the actual runtime contract. UserNotificationPreferences.channelConfigs was typed as Record<NotificationChannel, ChannelConfig> requiring all 7 channel keys to be present, but production reads via `prefs.channelConfigs?.[channel]` — i.e. treats it as PARTIAL at the access site. The mismatch forced every spec / caller to fill 5 dummy `enabled: false` entries to satisfy the over-strict declared shape.
notes: Closed by PR-38 (chore/channel-configs-partial-pr38). Changed UserNotificationPreferences.channelConfigs from Record<NotificationChannel, ChannelConfig> to Partial<Record<NotificationChannel, ChannelConfig>>. Behavior-preserving (production code reads via optional chain). Removed the makeChannelConfigs() helper that PR-36 added in apps/alert-engine/src/notification/__tests__/channel-router.service.spec.ts; tests now use natural literal subsets. alert-engine spec compile remains at 0.

title: Monorepo strictness divergence: noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature + isolatedModules applied per-project rather than uniformly via tsconfig.base.json
rule_violated: Compiler-strictness settings should live in tsconfig.base.json (single source of truth), not be repeated/diverged per project. Pre-PR-41 `isolatedModules` was set at 3 lib tsconfigs (farm-shared, shared-contracts, node-components) but missing from base — apps inheriting only base did not enforce it. PR-32 (libs/migration-harness) had to ADD an `isolatedModules: false` override on its tsconfig.spec.json to relax it because cross-lib imports tripped the stricter setting that migration-harness's own tsconfig.json applied. The asymmetric application meant strict-tsc results varied by which project did the compile.
notes: PR-41 closes PHASE 1 (isolatedModules monorepo-wide). isolatedModules: true added to tsconfig.base.json. 165 violations across 11 projects collapsed to 11 unique source files when traced (the same shared libs imported by every consumer). Fixed by converting type-only re-exports to `export type {…}` in: libs/backend-common/src/health/index.ts, libs/backend-common/src/index.ts (middleware + tenant-validating-consumer), libs/backend-common/src/logging/index.ts, libs/backend-common/src/pagination/index.ts (inline `type` modifier on IStandardPaginatedResult + IPaginatedResult), libs/event-contracts/src/upcasters/index.ts, libs/storage/src/index.ts, platform/libs/event-bus/src/index.ts (export type * from), apps/gateway-api/src/guards/auth.guard.ts, apps/sensor-service/src/vfd/adapters/index.ts (split class + interface re-exports for 7 protocol adapters), apps/sensor-service/src/vfd/entities/vfd-register-mapping.entity.ts, apps/admin-api-service/src/billing/services/subscription-management.service.ts (kept SubscriptionStatus enum as value re-export, split 11 interfaces to type-only), apps/admin-api-service/src/impersonation/services/debug-tools.service.ts. Also removed redundant `isolatedModules: false` override from libs/migration-harness/tsconfig.spec.json — no longer needed once base provides the setting and all violations are fixed. PHASE 2 (noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature monorepo-wide) is its own follow-up — the probe showed ~1100 violations dominated by `process.env.X` patterns that need a separate cleanup PR series. State stays IN-PROGRESS until phase 2 closes. Phase 2 closed by PR-42 (chore/no-property-access-from-index-signature-pr42). 1010 violations resolved across 97 unique files. Built tools/scripts/fix-no-property-access-from-index-signature.mjs — runs tsc, parses TS4111 line:col output, programmatically rewrites obj.foo to obj['foo'] (or obj?.['foo'] for optional chains). 855 rewrites in pass 1, 0 in pass 2 (converged). 59 follow-up regex fixes for the optional-chain edge case (script bug — was producing obj?['foo']; fixed in script for future runs). Setting added to tsconfig.base.json; redundant per-project overrides removed from libs/migration-harness. All 22 monorepo projects 0/0 green.

title: ORPHAN-HIGH-020 D-1b prep — SignedStSource primitive (canonical bytes + verify) for source-signature trust transfer
rule_violated: Ultra-plan D-1b ST source compile production wire (ORPHAN-HIGH-020). title: Faz 6 two-person integrity primitive — CommandEnvelope v3 co_approver_actor + co_approver_signature wire fields
rule_violated: Plan §5 Faz 6 + ADR-017 §8 two-person integrity. Pre-Batch-#305 the engine-side scaffolding existed (AuthorizationRequest.co_approver: Option<CoApproverEvidence> with PolicyEngine verifying co-approver permission + actor inequality + tenant binding) but the CommandEnvelope wire format had NO co-approver fields. Architectural fix: v3 wire format extension. Two new optional fields on CommandEnvelope: co_approver_actor: Option<[u8; 16]> + co_approver_signature: Option<Ed25519SignatureBytes>. Domain separator tag bumped 'command-envelope-sig-v2' → 'command-envelope-sig-v3'. Co-approver signature signs the SAME canonical-bytes transcript as primary; an attacker who mutates any field post-co-approval invalidates BOTH signatures. The architectural shape rejects the 'co-approver signs different canonical subset' alternative: signing the SAME bytes means an attacker cannot mutate anything post-co-approval without invalidating BOTH sigs, AND there is one signed transcript to audit (no two-transcript reconciliation problem). title: Faz 2 D-2 partial — mlock pin process pages in RAM via mlockall(MCL_CURRENT|MCL_FUTURE) (memfd_secret + panic_zeroize registry land in #310 + #311)
rule_violated: Plan §5 Faz 2 D-2 + ADR-018 §7 + ADR-019 §5 in-process hardening. Pre-Batch-#309 the process_hardening module installed prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0) (Layer B — kernel-level coredump suppression) + panic-abort hook (Layer D — no destructor unwinding on panic) but the master keystore pages had NO mlockall guarantee — kernel could page secret bytes (master key, derived per-purpose keys, envelope signature material) to swap under memory pressure. An attacker with post-reboot forensic access to the swap partition (eMMC dump, cloud-VM hypervisor escape) could extract the master key from a paged-out copy even though the in-RAM copy was correctly drop-zeroized. Architectural fix: new process_hardening::mlock submodule wrapping mlockall(MCL_CURRENT | MCL_FUTURE) — locks every current page AND every future allocation including async stack frames + heap regrowth. Idempotent (kernel ignores second call), structured error taxonomy (NotPermitted/InsufficientLimit/TemporaryFailure/UnknownErrno/UnsupportedPlatform) discriminating the EPERM/ENOMEM/EAGAIN/other errno classes, MlockState{locked_current, locked_future} return shape captures the actual posture for audit emission, proc_self_vm_locked_bytes() audit accessor parses /proc/self/status VmLck for runtime verification + future observability metrics. Wired into harden_process() boot sequence BEFORE panic-hook install (idempotent ordering — both calls are commutative). Best-effort by default (mlock requires CAP_IPC_LOCK or sufficient RLIMIT_MEMLOCK; container envs often lack this); structured warn log with operator-readable diagnostic when mlockall fails, future config.security.mlock_enforce flag will fail-close boot. Architectural property: complements existing zeroize-on-drop layer at the keystore::secret module — secrets are scrubbed when the value drops AND no copy of the page reaches swap while the value is alive. Choosing mlockall over selective mlock is intentional: secret bytes can transiently appear on async stack frames between awaits which are not addressable from the secret's owner, AND Rust's allocator may freely move heap allocations across pages requiring re-mlock per realloc. Pinning the entire address space is the only architecturally honest answer for a Rust-async process; memory cost on RPi CM4 (1-8 GB RAM) is acceptable since the agent's working set is ~150-300 MB at p99.
notes: First slice of the D-2 arc. 5 new unit tests pin: MlockError Display strings (audit-stable identifiers — operator dashboards key on these), MlockState field shape (audit consumers don't see silent breakage), MlockError implements std::error::Error (? interop), mlock_all_pages on Linux returns structured Result with MlockState{locked_current=true,locked_future=true} on success OR a structured Err (no panic; CI runners typically lack CAP_IPC_LOCK so both branches are acceptable test outcomes), proc_self_vm_locked_bytes returns Some on Linux + None on non-Linux. Default-feature suite tests: 1795/1795 passing (1790 prior + 5 new; zero regression). NOT IN THIS BATCH (the D-2 arc has 3 batches; the next two land follow-on slices closing ULTRA-HIGH-016 D-2): Batch #310 = memfd_secret(2) primitive (Linux 5.14+) + SecretRegion abstraction giving keystore::secret a strongest-class container whose pages cannot be mapped into other processes (even root can't read /proc/PID/mem); Batch #311 = panic_zeroize registry that walks registered secret regions zeroing them BEFORE std::process::abort() so panics scrub known secrets even when destructors don't run. The architectural shape pinned here (mlock submodule with its own error taxonomy + state-result type) is the template for the next two batches' submodules (process_hardening::memfd_secret + process_hardening::panic_zeroize). NO Cargo.toml dep changes (libc 0.2 was already in deps). ORPHAN FINDING NOTED (carried over from Batch #307+#308): ORPHAN-LOW-028 sens-api-gateway/src/main.rs.disabled-test 37-byte stub still untouched.

title: Faz 2 D-2 partial — memfd_secret(2) primitive (Linux 5.14+) MemfdSecretRegion strongest in-process secret container (panic_zeroize lands in #311)
rule_violated: Plan §5 Faz 2 D-2 + ADR-018 §7 + ADR-019 §5 in-process hardening — memfd_secret slice. Pre-Batch-#310 the in-process defense layers were: prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0) (Layer B, kernel-level coredump suppression), mlockall (Batch #309 Layer C, pages off swap), panic-abort hook (Layer D, no destructor unwinding on panic), zeroize-on-drop (Layer E, scrub at value drop). Critical gap: NONE of those prevent (a) /proc/<pid>/mem reads from a privileged process post-compromise, (b) hibernation image inclusion via swsusp, (c) live-migration / VM snapshot inclusion via KVM. Architectural fix: new process_hardening::memfd_secret submodule wrapping the Linux 5.14+ memfd_secret(2) syscall. Pages allocated through MemfdSecretRegion are excluded from ALL of: kernel direct-map (the kernel itself cannot reach them outside the owning process via set_direct_map_invalid_noflush()), /proc/<pid>/mem (kernel rejects reads on memfd_secret VMAs), hibernation images (swsusp skips), KVM guest RAM dumps (host hypervisor cannot snapshot). MemfdSecretRegion owns (fd, ptr, len) tuple with manual unsafe Send (no aliasing — exclusive ownership), NOT Sync (matches Vec<u8>'s exclusivity model — &mut self required for write access; callers needing shared access wrap in Mutex). Drop impl munmaps + closes; kernel automatically zeroes pages on release. Constructor allocate(len) rejects len==0 with structured ZeroLength variant; runtime probe is_supported() returns bool (one syscall + close, ENOSYS detection). Fallback path: when kernel < 5.14 or built without CONFIG_SECRETMEM, allocate() returns Err(NotSupported); caller falls back to mlock + anonymous-mmap path (Batch #309). Architectural property pinned: 'secrets in memfd_secret OR mlock-pinned' is the contract; the caller picks the strongest available. Manual Debug impl REDACTS contents (no byte hex leak in formatted output).
notes: Second slice of the D-2 arc (after Batch #309 mlock primitive). 8 new unit tests pin: MemfdSecretError Display strings (audit-stable identifiers), error implements std::error::Error, ZeroLength rejection at constructor boundary, is_supported probe returns bool no-panic env-independent, allocate round-trip with kernel-zeroed initial state + write+read parity for 64 bytes (executes only when is_supported() == true; on this dev env Linux 6.8.0 + syscall 447 = supported), multiple regions coexist isolated, MemfdSecretRegion: Send compile-time check, Debug impl REDACTS (no byte hex leak even after fill(0xde)). Default-feature suite tests: 1803/1803 passing (1795 prior + 8 new; zero regression). Architectural decision pinned in module doc: choosing memfd_secret over mlock+plain-mmap is correct WHEN the kernel supports it because mlock alone does not close /proc/<pid>/mem reads, hibernation includes mlock pages, VM snapshots see mlock pages — only memfd_secret excludes from all three surfaces. NOT IN THIS BATCH: panic_zeroize registry (Batch #311) — global lock-guarded registry of secret regions that the panic hook walks zeroing each region BEFORE std::process::abort() so panics scrub known secrets even when destructors don't run. Replaces the current panic-abort hook with panic-zeroize-then-abort. After #311 the D-2 arc is fully closed (ULTRA-HIGH-016 D-2 candidate for closure). NO Cargo.toml dep changes (libc 0.2 already in deps; SYS_memfd_secret + libc::syscall are stable surface). NO existing-keystore consumer wiring yet — keystore::secret will adopt MemfdSecretRegion as its master backing store in a future Sprint 6.4 batch (after the panic_zeroize registry lands so panics scrub the master too). ORPHAN FINDING NOTED (carried over): ORPHAN-LOW-028 main.rs.disabled-test 37-byte stub still untouched.

title: Faz 2 D-2 closure — panic_zeroize registry walks registered secret regions zeroing each BEFORE std::process::abort() (closes ULTRA-HIGH-016 D-2 arc with #309+#310+#311)
rule_violated: Plan §5 Faz 2 D-2 + ADR-018 §7 + ADR-019 §5 in-process hardening — panic_zeroize slice + arc closure. Pre-Batch-#311 the in-process defense layer cake was: prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0) (Layer B), mlockall (Batch #309 Layer C), memfd_secret (Batch #310 Layer C+, when supported), zeroize-on-drop (Layer E), panic-abort hook (Layer D). CRITICAL GAP: between the panic instant and the kernel-reap, secret pages are still mapped + readable by a concurrent thread / by the kernel itself reading process memory. On a panicking multi-threaded program the panic hook runs on ONE thread; OTHER threads continue running until abort() actually fires. That window is small but architecturally non-zero. Architectural fix: new process_hardening::panic_zeroize submodule providing a global registry of (NonNull<u8>, usize) secret regions with register/unregister/scrub-all surface. The panic-abort hook now walks the registry zeroing each region BEFORE std::process::abort(), shrinking the window to 'during the zeroize loop'. Best-effort with try_lock + 100ms deadline so a panic mid-register/unregister does not deadlock the hook (in that rare case the kernel still releases pages on process exit + the mlock + zeroize-on-drop layers remain in effect — defense-in-depth optimization, not primary guarantee). OnceLock + Mutex<Vec<RegisteredRegion>> shape: lazy init keeps no-secret-allocation programs zero-cost; Mutex serializes register/unregister/scrub access; poison-recovery via into_inner() means a previous lock-holder's panic doesn't break registration for survivors. Raw pointers (NonNull<u8>) chosen over references because the registry is 'static + the secret regions have shorter lifetimes that no single 'a satisfies; caller register/unregister pairing is the documented contract. Manual unsafe Send on RegisteredRegion: pointer + length values are integers; moving the slot is safe under the caller's region-validity contract. test_only_clear() crate-private accessor lets test fixtures reset between cases without exposing a production reset API. title: Faz 2 D-1b persistence — RotationMarkerStore atomic-write JSON marker for cross-restart last_rotation_at tracking
rule_violated: Plan §5 Faz 2 D-1b + ADR-018 §6 cross-restart rotation tracking. Pre-Batch-#316 the Batch #315 KeystoreRotationDeadline was a process-bound in-memory primitive with NO persistence. A deadline that resets to 'now' on every reboot would never fire (operators rebooting weekly would never see an Overdue alarm regardless of the actual rotation history) — fundamental defeat of the alarm contract. Architectural fix: new keystore::rotation_marker_store module providing atomic-write JSON persistence under $SUDERRA_DATA_DIR/keystore_rotation_marker.json. Three operations: read_marker(path) -> Option<KeystoreRotationDeadline> (None on missing file = first-boot signal; Err on I/O failure or corruption); write_marker(path, &deadline) atomic via temp-file + fsync + rename (POSIX same-fs rename atomicity); read_or_init(path, clock, init_factory) boot-path entry that reads existing OR mints + persists fresh deadline. record_rotation_now(path, &mut deadline, clock) is the post-rotation update sequence: advance in-memory THEN persist (if persistence fails the in-memory deadline IS NOT advanced — fail-closed against silent rotation-missed scenario). Schema-versioned wire format (schema_version field in JSON) so future schema changes can land without breaking older readers (forward-incompat returns SchemaVersionMismatch). Structured MarkerStoreError taxonomy: ReadFailed (file unreadable I/O), WriteFailed (atomic-write sequence broken), Corrupt (JSON parse), SchemaVersionMismatch (forward-incompat), Deadline(RotationDeadlineError) (wraps the underlying ctor failures from KeystoreRotationDeadline::new_with_defaults). Why JSON over bincode/SQLCipher: marker is operator-readable (incident-response engineers cat the file to see the timestamp); single i64 with no key material so no security gain from encrypted storage; schema_version field gates evolution. Why separate module from rotation_deadline.rs: pure-domain type stays free of I/O dependencies for unit-test boundary cleanliness; same architectural pattern as keystore::secret (pure types) + keystore::file_backed (I/O + ctor) split from Batch 4b/82.

Three new public methods: open_with_rotation_tracker(passphrase, salt, params, acceptance, marker_path, clock) - async ctor that calls rotation_marker_store::read_or_init (first-boot mints + persists via the closure-injected KeystoreRotationDeadline::new_with_defaults factory; subsequent boots read existing); rotation_status() - async accessor returning Option<Result<RotationStatus, RotationDeadlineError>> (None when tracker not wired, Some(Ok) when wired + evaluation succeeded, Some(Err) when clock or marker error surfaces); rotate_master_from_files_with_tracking(passphrase, salt, params) - async wrapper that calls the existing sync rotate_master_from_files for the actual master swap, then on success acquires the deadline write guard + calls rotation_marker_store::record_rotation_now. Critical architectural decision: FAIL-SAFE error semantic on marker write failure post-master-swap. If the master swap succeeds but the marker persistence fails, the in-memory master IS the new one but the persisted marker is stale by one rotation — log warn + return Ok. The alarm runner fires too EARLY on the next tick (operator runs ceremony, alarm clears) - preferable to too LATE (silent rotation miss). Per ADR-018 §6 fail-safe doctrine. Lock kind discipline: master uses std::sync::RwLock (sync; argon2 compute is sync); deadline uses tokio::sync::RwLock (async; record_rotation_now crosses awaits). Mixed lock kinds in same struct is the architecturally honest shape - each field gets the lock kind matching its access pattern. Legacy open() ctor preserved with rotation_tracker=None: tests + dev-mode boots that don't care about the alarm chain pay no read_or_init / clock-injection cost.

title: OPC UA SessionLease decrement-on-close depends on TTL fail-safe; no async-opcua session-close callback hook (Phase B-3 architectural decision)
evidence: sens-api-gateway/src/opc_ua_sens_auth_manager.rs (active_leases per-token registry — placeholder for future hook)
rule_violated: RAII SessionLease should release on actual session-close; async-opcua 0.18 AuthManager trait does not expose a session-close callback at this layer — same architectural class as ORPHAN-HIGH-045 + ORPHAN-MEDIUM-051
notes: Phase B-3 lands per-tenant + per-user quota with TTL=1h fail-safe release. SessionLease Drop fires on the SensAuthManager-side scope exit; for sessions held by async-opcua's internal session pool, the Drop only fires when the SensAuthManager itself drops. The active_leases per-token registry is the architectural placeholder for a future Phase B-3.5 wire that hooks async-opcua's session-close (when the upstream API exposes it) — the registry will be drained by token on close, and Drop fires explicitly. Until then, TTL=1h aligns with OPC UA secure-channel renewal cadence (a session that doesn't explicitly release its lease evicts within 1h). Closure path: same as ORPHAN-HIGH-045 (per-handshake reject hook) + ORPHAN-MEDIUM-051 (ClientAddr exposure) — fixing one likely fixes all three (single async-opcua API extension exposing session lifecycle hooks).

Fix: per-connection watermark (lastSyncAtRef, advanced on live newMessage); first-connect vs reconnect via hasConnectedRef; on reconnect drain allMessagesSince(since=watermark) paginated by syncToken, upsert via shared upsertMessageIntoChannelCache (same helper as live newMessage), invalidate channel-list + unread-count badges; isReconcilingRef guard; failure leaves watermark for next-reconnect retry.

title: messaging unread count disagrees between the Redis HASH counter (excludes sender) and the get-channels DB subquery (no senderId filter, includes own messages) on a member's own messages

title: NATS client is nats.js v2 (maintenance mode); v3 @nats-io/* is a hard package split that cannot be alias-swapped (JSONCodec blocker) — PR-A migrates the 12 direct importers, v2 retained for @nestjs/microservices pending PR-B
evidence: platform/libs/event-bus/src/nats/nats-event-bus.ts (1002-line transactional event bus; primary v2 importer migrated to @nats-io/transport-node+nats-core+jetstream)
platform/libs/event-bus/src/nats/nats-request-reply.ts (request/reply helper; ErrorCode/NatsError removed in v3 -> TimeoutError/NoRespondersError)
node_modules/@nestjs/microservices/serializers/nats-record.serializer.js:11 (require('nats').JSONCodec() — the runtime hard-blocker forcing a staged migration, v3 removed JSONCodec)
package.json (added @nats-io/transport-node + nats-core + jetstream ^3.4.0; nats 2.x retained for @nestjs/microservices until PR-B)
rule_violated: A maintenance-mode runtime dependency carrying the platform event bus must migrate to the maintained line (@nats-io/* 3.x). The @nestjs/microservices JSONCodec runtime dependency on nats v2 makes a single alias swap fatal, so the migration is staged: PR-A (direct importers) -> PR-B (platform CustomTransportStrategy/ClientProxy) -> PR-C (remove v2 + ban).
notes: PR-A (this commit): additive v3-alongside-v2. Added @nats-io/{transport-node,nats-core,jetstream}@^3.4.0 + lockfile; migrated 12 direct importers (9 source + 3 test) to v3. StringCodec/JSONCodec removed -> publish(string)/respond(string)/request(string) + msg.string()/msg.json() (byte-identical UTF-8 wire); jetstream(nc)/jetstreamManager(nc) function form; ErrorCode+NatsError -> TimeoutError/NoRespondersError; JsMsg.info.redeliveryCount -> deliveryCount (pure rename, v2 already @deprecated; backoff math preserved). buildNatsConnectionOptions (ADR-015 anchor) untouched; client-agnostic, no nats import. VERIFICATION: a standalone v3-API smoke-test type-checked (tsc) against the extracted real @nats-io/*@3.4.0 .d.ts = EXIT 0 (caught the redeliveryCount->deliveryCount removal, a latent 2x-backoff regression had it been renamed naively); leftover-scan clean across all 12 files; per-file adversarial verify via workflow fan-out. @nats-io not in worktree node_modules (like @nestjs/apollo) -> full compile delegated to GitHub CI. NOT done (separate PRs): PR-B platform CustomTransportStrategy/ClientProxy wire-compat cutover of ~14 ClientsModule.register sites + create-service-app.ts (golden-envelope fixtures BEFORE v2 removal); PR-C remove nats 2.x + no-restricted-imports ban + dependency invariant.

title: Platform libs lack a selected eslint-project tsconfig; lib files importing exports-only packages (e.g. @nats-io/*) type-resolve to any/error under @typescript-eslint, producing no-unsafe-* false positives
evidence: platform/libs/event-bus/src/nats/nats-event-bus.ts (connect() no-unsafe-assignment is a verified false positive; documented eslint-disable points to this finding)
.eslintrc.json (parserOptions.project lists tsconfig.base.json first and match-all, so it is selected over per-project tsconfigs for platform lib files)
tsconfig.base.json (no include -> matches all .ts; moduleResolution:node cannot resolve @nats-io exports-only ESM, broken types:.d.js field)
rule_violated: eslint type-aware lint must resolve a file against a project where its node_modules dependencies resolve. parserOptions.project selection order (base first + match-all) causes platform lib files to be type-checked standalone against bare tsconfig.base.json, where exports-only ESM packages do not resolve.
notes: Surfaced by A3 (first platform lib to import @nats-io). The code is type-correct: platform-wide type-check + build + event-bus unit tests all pass (consumer/app context resolves @nats-io). Six fixes attempted in A3 (NodeConnectionOptions, whole-spread, tsconfig paths, type-derivation-from-connect, esModuleInterop, dedicated lib tsconfig) — none dislodge tsconfig.base from being selected first by parserOptions.project. Proper fix (highest tier): reorder parserOptions.project so per-project globs precede tsconfig.base.json (or drop base if every linted file is covered) — a cross-cutting eslint-config change to validate against the full lint surface, out of scope for the NATS migration. Documented eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-assignment at the connect() call cites this finding; removable once the project-order fix lands.

title: postgres-protocol 0.6.11 + tokio-postgres 0.7.17 carry newly-published RustSec advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0178/0179/0180: SCRAM-iteration CPU-DoS + DataRow/hstore decode panics) that red-line cargo-audit + cargo-deny on every Rust PR repo-wide
evidence: Cargo.lock (postgres-protocol 0.6.11, tokio-postgres 0.7.17, postgres-types 0.2.13 — the affected versions)
crates/outbox-rs/Cargo.toml:48 (tokio-postgres = '0.7' direct dep; range already permits the patched 0.7.18, so a lockfile bump suffices)
.cargo/audit.toml (ignore = [] — advisories are denied, so cargo-audit + cargo-deny fail repo-wide until the bump lands)
rule_violated: A newly-published high-severity RustSec advisory on a transitive dependency must be remediated by upgrading to the patched release (RUSTSEC policy: ignore only with owner+deadline when no fix exists). A fix exists (postgres-protocol >=0.6.12, tokio-postgres >=0.7.18), so the correct action is a lockfile bump, not an ignore.
notes: Surfaced gating R1's Rust CI (#450): both cargo-audit and cargo-deny (advisories check) fail on RUSTSEC-2026-0179 (HIGH 8.7, SCRAM unbounded-iteration CPU-DoS) + 0180 (MEDIUM, hstore decode panic) on postgres-protocol 0.6.11, and RUSTSEC-2026-0178 (MEDIUM, DataRow panic) on tokio-postgres 0.7.17. Main predates the advisory publication so its last rust-ci runs were green; every Rust PR now red-lines. Fixed by `cargo update -p tokio-postgres --precise 0.7.18` + `-p postgres-protocol --precise 0.6.12` (cascades postgres-types 0.2.14) — patched versions, no ignore. Only the root workspace is affected; sens-api-gateway does not depend on these crates.

title: createUser non-transactional dual-write — UserInvited routed through BestEffortEventPublisher (lossy-allowlisted) instead of the durable transactional outbox until user-creation is wrapped in a single transaction
evidence: apps/auth-service/src/modules/tenant/services/user-lifecycle.service.ts:128 (createUser entry — not wrapped in a single transaction)
rule_violated: DATA-HIGH-001 durable-event policy: a state-change event must be enqueued in the same transaction as the state write (transactional outbox). createUser is not transactional, so its UserInvited cannot be durably enqueued and remains best-effort (lossy-allowlisted).
notes: Dangling-reference seed (Tier-4, 2026-06-14): ORPHAN-HIGH-090 was referenced by id in the DATA-HIGH-001 resolution prose AND in production code (best-effort-event-publisher.ts:65) but had NO registry entry — a traceability gap (the number was consumed by prose/code before it was seeded). Surfaced during W3.3 outbox adoption (PR #390, DATA-HIGH-001): every other durable auth domain event was moved into the transactional outbox; UserInvited from user-lifecycle createUser is the sole remaining best-effort path because user creation is not wrapped in one transaction. The invitation row is itself a durable record (a lost event is recoverable by an admin re-sending the pending invite), so this is NOT a data-loss vector — but it sits below the durable-outbox bar. How-to-fix: wrap createUser (entity save + side effects) in a single dataSource.transaction, then upgrade UserInvited to OutboxPublisher.enqueue(event, manager) mirroring UserDeleted/TenantStatusChanged, and remove UserInvited from the BestEffortEventPublisher ALLOWLIST once durable.

title: nx affected --target=lint OOMs on Nx projects lacking a scoped parser tsconfig (non-provenance projects fall through to the monorepo-wide TS_PROJECTS glob), making the lint gate unrunnable and masking accumulated lint debt
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md CRITICAL — `nx affected --target=lint` must run green as the CI quality gate; typed-lint parserOptions.project must be scoped per project, not the monorepo-wide TS_PROJECTS glob.
notes: Heap OOM observed on migration-harness, aquaculture-engines, service-catalog during nx affected lint. Fix adds NON_PROVENANCE_TS_PROJECTS in eslint.config.mjs scoping parserOptions.project per non-provenance project to its own tsconfig.eslint.json. title: Single-node NATS cannot recover the R3 AQUACULTURE_EVENTS JetStream stream because replica count was bound to NODE_ENV (production=>3) instead of NATS topology; the standalone droplet demanded a 3-replica stream it cannot host, failing the JetStream health check and cascading every depends_on-gated service into a stuck Created state
rule_violated: ADR-016 deploy-resilience + CLAUDE.md root-cause SSoT: JetStream replica count is a NATS topology property (cluster node count), not an application-environment property; durability is owned by the transactional outbox + event-store, so JetStream R-factor is transport HA only and must never produce a stream the connected server cannot host.
notes: Fix decouples replica count from NODE_ENV (default 1), removes the production-must-be-3 throw, and clamps num_replicas to the connected server topology (standalone => 1) via ServerInfo.cluster in setupStream(), making an unrecoverable stream structurally impossible. Recovery also clears the corrupt R3 stream dir from the nats_data volume (zero-loss; outbox replays).

title: sensor-service publishes SensorReading/ParentReadingRouted fire-and-forget (circuit-breaker, swallowed) instead of via its transactional outbox; alert-engine consumes SensorReading event-driven, so a dropped event silently skips alert evaluation — a missed life-safety alert (e.g. dissolved-oxygen crash)

title: farm task.create and recurring-task generation publish domain events directly (create after save outside tx; recurring + overdue-cron after save / under autocommit) while task.update already enqueues via the transactional outbox — the inconsistency loses events on a crash or NATS gap

title: Tenant DB boundary (runInTenantRead/runInTenantTransaction) pins search_path but never sets or asserts app.current_tenant / current_schema(), so a lost tenant context (unset RLS GUC) or a missing tenant schema yields a silent empty / wrong-schema read instead of a hard error

notes: Boundary now sets app.current_tenant tx-local and asserts current_schema() + GUC against expected tenant_<uuid>, throwing TenantContextError (SCHEMA_MISMATCH/RLS_MISMATCH). Handler migration onto the asserting boundary tracked under the farm-data-ssot plan.

title: Farm write/command handlers ran transactions via bare createQueryRunner without pinning search_path or asserting the RLS GUC
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach — tenant-owned writes must run through runInTenantTransaction so search_path is pinned + the RLS GUC asserted, instead of relying on pool-checkout state
notes: 21 write/command handlers migrated from bare this.dataSource.createQueryRunner() + manual connect/startTransaction/commit/rollback/release onto runInTenantTransaction(this.dataSource, 'farm', command.tenantId, ...). Constructors unchanged. Transactional-outbox enqueue(event, queryRunner.manager) calls and auditLog.logWithManager preserved INSIDE the callback (atomic with writes); the single post-commit logger.log in transfer-batch moved to after the wrapper resolves; mobile-command replay early-returns converted (wrapper commits the read-only tx). Specs converted to createMockDataSource (banned as-unknown-as casts removed); farm-service tsconfig.spec type-check clean; full handler/resolver suite 362 tests green. allocate-to-tank deferred (SERIALIZABLE isolation) — tracked as FARM-HIGH-079. With this, 21/22 farm write handlers and all eligible read handlers route through the fail-closed boundary.

title: allocate-to-tank still runs a bare SERIALIZABLE transaction outside the tenant boundary; runInTenantTransaction cannot express an explicit isolation level
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach — this critical concurrent-allocation write path still does not pin search_path or assert the RLS GUC; the boundary helper lacks an isolation-level option so migrating would silently downgrade SERIALIZABLE to READ COMMITTED
notes: allocate-to-tank.handler.ts uses startTransaction('SERIALIZABLE') as a deliberate concurrency-control choice (per its SECURITY FIX header) to prevent races when multiple requests allocate to the same tank. runInTenantTransaction always uses the connection default (READ COMMITTED), so migrating as-is would downgrade isolation — forbidden behavior change on a write path. Remediation: extend runInTenantTransaction with an optional isolation-level parameter (or add a runInTenantSerializableTransaction variant) that pins search_path + asserts the RLS GUC AND honors SERIALIZABLE, then migrate allocate-to-tank. Until then this path retains its bare boundary and is NOT search_path-pinned / GUC-asserted.

notes: Removed tenant-rls.service.ts + its spec; dropped from RlsModule.forPoolService providers/exports, rls/index.ts barrel, and the doc comments; updated a stale reference comment in rls-connection-bootstrap.service.ts. Verified zero remaining references repo-wide. rls.module.spec provider-count assertions decremented (TenantRlsService no longer registered) and the TenantRlsService-specific test cases removed. The canonical RLS form lives in apply-tenant-rls.helper.ts (NULLIF(...)) and the runtime GUC is set/asserted by RlsConnectionBootstrap + the tenant read/write boundary. title: No sanctioned source-read API for cross-tenant reference/federation reads; get-farm federation read + system/farm resolvers masked lost tenant context as null/[]

notes: Added runInSourceRead(dataSource, sourceSchema, fn) + assertSourceReadContext to the boundary SSoT: a READ ONLY tx that pins search_path to the source schema, sets app.bypass_rls='on' transaction-locally (cross-tenant by design), and asserts current_schema()===sourceSchema (stray tenant schema → SCHEMA_MISMATCH). get-farm migrated to a hybrid: tenant path → runInTenantRead, federation __resolveReference (no tenantId) → runInSourceRead. Removed the error-masking catch→null/[] in system.resolver (parentSystem now catches only NotFoundException; childSystemsField drops the try/catch since ListSystems returns []) and farm.resolver resolveReference (catches only NotFoundException) so a TenantContextError surfaces instead of becoming a silent null/empty. get-farm removed from the read-boundary arch-test allowlist. Specs added (assertSourceReadContext ×4, get-farm ×3); full farm-service handler/resolver suite 365 tests green; farm-service tsconfig.spec type-check clean. Remaining allowlist: get-batch-performance (service-delegating), get-equipment-types/get-sub-equipment-types (per-tenant catalogs read via request-context tenantId — #9 tail), list-equipment (mixed), storage cursor primitive.
