title: Outbox WORKER DISPATCH is fail-open on tenantId (tenant-less payload mis-routed to events.system.* instead of dead-lettered) in @platform/outbox
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach — a tenant-scoped event missing its tenantId at dispatch must fail closed (dead-letter), not be mis-routed to the system subject; root-cause is in the shared @platform/outbox worker
notes: TRACKED (no code change this cycle: shared-lib + nuanced). ENQUEUE already fail-closed (OutboxPublisher.enqueue rejects missing/blank/non-UUID tenantId; every farm handler uses it). DISPATCH fail-open: publishLeasedBatch publishes row.payload and deriveSubject routes a tenant-less payload to events.system.{eventType}. Blanket reject would break legitimate tenant-less SYSTEM events, so the fix needs a tenant-scoped-vs-system distinction in @platform/outbox (platform-team change): assert tenant-scoped events carry a UUID tenantId before publish, dead-letter on failure; consider OutboxEntityBase.tenantId NOT NULL once backfilled. Scope-adjacent: farm direct eventBus.publish() callsites bypass the outbox without a tenantId guard.

title: No invariant enforced that farm NATS event handlers establish a tenant context before DB access
rule_violated: Farm Data SSOT plan section 4-2 — every NATS event handler doing DB work must wrap in withTenantContext (no HTTP request context exists); the convention was unenforced after FARM-CRITICAL-060/FARM-HIGH-067
notes: New always-on invariant (layer-3 shard): scans apps/farm-service/src for NATS handlers (implements IEventHandler + bus subscribe/subscribeWildcard), requires each DB-touching handler to reference withTenantContext / runInTenantTransaction / runInTenantRead (or an explicit SET search_path on a dedicated runner). 5 handlers found, all compliant → passes today; allowlist empty (+ honesty test). In-process @OnEvent listeners are out of scope (separate dead-listener invariant). Wired into tests/invariants/jest.config.ts.

title: post-deploy verification had no semantic farm-contract canary (smoke only)
rule_violated: Farm Data SSOT plan section 3-G/16 — deploy verification must assert a real farm GraphQL contract through the public edge, not just HTTP 200
notes: Added a semantic canary: a named farm GraphQL read (`{ farms { id } }`) through public nginx /graphql asserts (1) 200 + parseable envelope, (2) the supergraph KNOWS the farms field (composition check — GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED → farm subgraph not composed → FAIL), (3) an anonymous caller gets NO farm data AND a UNAUTHENTICATED/FORBIDDEN error (data-without-auth → CRITICAL isolation breach → FAIL). Uses python3 + existing PUBLIC_SMOKE_* env vars (no secrets/hostnames hardcoded; production disables introspection so a negative-contract probe is the correct shape check). bash -n clean.

title: nginx edge did not propagate/log a correlation-id, blocking end-to-end nginx→gateway→farm trace
rule_violated: Farm Data SSOT plan section 4-7/18 — a single request must be traceable across nginx, gateway and farm logs via a shared correlation-id
notes: nginx now preserves an incoming x-correlation-id (the exact header gateway-api/correlation-id.middleware.ts reads) or generates $request_id, passes it upstream, and includes it in the json access log so the edge line shares the id the gateway/StructuredLogger use. CSP/x-tenant/HMAC header handling preserved. TRACKED gap: the production droplet edge infrastructure/nginx/droplet.conf still lacks the change (out of the permitted scope this cycle) — apply the same correlation-id block there.

title: No Grafana dashboard/alerts for the farm tenant-read-boundary signals
rule_violated: Farm Data SSOT plan section 3-G/20 — farm mutation/outbox/boundary metrics need an owned dashboard + alerts with runbook_url
notes: Added a 'Farm Data SSOT / Tenant Boundary' dashboard (farm_mutation_* + outbox depth/age panels) matching the existing dashboard schema/datasource, and Prometheus alert rules (elevated farm mutation error rate, outbox backlog/age) with runbook_url annotations, in prometheus/alerts/ next to slo-alerts.yml. Dashboard JSON + alerts YAML validated. Any referenced metric not yet emitted is noted in the dashboard as a TODO panel.

title: Test-only RLS GUC-name drift: specs asserted app.current_tenant_id (nothing sets it) vs canonical app.current_tenant
rule_violated: Farm Data SSOT plan section 2/21 — tests must assert the canonical runtime RLS GUC (app.current_tenant via NULLIF), not a drifted name
notes: Corrected the test-only GUC name app.current_tenant_id → app.current_tenant (RLS_TENANT_GUC, the name the runtime actually sets) in the two integration specs so they assert the real contract. Runtime helper (apply-tenant-rls.helper.ts) was already canonical — no runtime change. TRACKED: an ARCHIVED observability migration still uses non-canonical app.platform_role, but it is dead code outside the active migration chain (left as-is; documented). These integration specs are env-gated (need Postgres), not run in the unit lane here.

title: No E2E proving the tenant-swap attack defense (forged x-tenant-id / swapped reference) end to end
rule_violated: Farm Data SSOT plan section 4-8/17 — a tenant-swap attack (forged header, swapped reference) must be proven to yield isolation (not a 200-empty), with the HMAC→RLS→response chain asserted
notes: Added e2e/tests/tenant-swap-attack.e2e.spec.ts: attacker (tenant A) reading tenant B farms gets zero B rows (not a silent 200-empty); forged x-tenant-id on an A token does not expose B; swapped-reference read is isolated; HMAC binds tenantId so a tampered binding is rejected. Env-gated (TENANT_SWAP_ATTACK_E2E=1 + live stack) exactly like sibling e2e specs — skips clean (3 skipped, 5 control tests pass) without the stack, so it never red-fails CI in stack-less envs.

title: Tenant DB boundary had no per-execution structured trace (resultState taxonomy) for read routing observability
rule_violated: Farm Data SSOT plan section 3-F/8.7 — the tenant boundary (the single chokepoint) should emit one structured trace per execution so a read's tenant routing + resultState is observable end to end
notes: runInTenantRead/runInTenantTransaction/runInSourceRead now emit one structured TenantBoundaryTrace per execution: { operation, resultState (SUCCESS|SCHEMA_MISMATCH|RLS_MISMATCH|ERROR), sourceSchema, expectedSchema, resolvedSchema, tenantHash (sha256/12 — raw tenant id never logged), correlationId, traceId (from getRequestContext), durationMs, rowCount (best-effort for array/paginated shapes) }. SUCCESS is debug-level (off in prod by default); a context mismatch is warn-level. The emit is fully wrapped in try/catch so observability can never break a read. Boundary-level (the §8.7 chokepoint), not per-handler. 11 boundary + 25 handler tests green; tsc + eslint clean.

title: No gate prevented new farm-module production mock-data imports from spreading
rule_violated: Farm Data SSOT plan section 5-5 — non-test farm source importing mock data must be a detectable, shrink-only set (tier-3) so the 'data appears/disappears' mock source cannot grow
notes: Added a NO-GROW ratchet invariant: the set of non-test farm-module files importing a mock module is frozen (10 files, all under pages/reports/); a NEW mock import fails the build, and the baseline-honesty test forces a removed entry to be deleted (shrink-only). Wired into the layer-3 shard. This is the tier-3 half; the tier-1 removal is FARM-HIGH-084.

title: Audit remediation: feeding-program resolver masked TenantContextError as null/[]; useHarvestPlans invalidation predicate missed tenant-scoped keys; boundary success-trace broke a debug-count test
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach — resolvers must not mask a lost tenant context as an empty result; tenant cache invalidation must match the tenant-scoped key shape; an observability addition must not change handler behavior/tests
notes: Three real gaps the completion-audit workflow caught, now fixed: (1) feeding-program.resolver.ts handleError() (used by 6 query resolvers) + tanksByProgram field resolver swallowed ALL errors to null/[] — they now re-throw TenantContextError (the same de-masking applied to system/farm resolvers in FARM-HIGH-080), so a lost tenant context surfaces instead of becoming a silent empty. (2) useHarvestPlans invalidateAllHarvestPlanQueries used predicate queryKey[0]==='harvestPlans' but tenant-scoped keys are ['tenant',tenantId,'harvestPlans',...] so it matched NOTHING (harvest plans stale across tenant switch); switched to createTenantInvalidationKey(tenantId,'harvestPlans'). (3) the FARM-MEDIUM-087 boundary SUCCESS trace (debug) added a debug call to every read and broke create-harvest-record's debug-count assertion; success trace is now OPT-IN behind FARM_DATA_READ_TRACE=on (mismatch warn stays always-on). Full farm handler/resolver/dataloader suite 365 green; farm-service + farm-module tsc clean. NOTE: the 2 rls.module.spec DI failures the gate-runner flagged are PRE-EXISTING on origin/main (verified), not from this branch.

title: Farm-service services swallowed tenant-read errors to null/[]/default, re-masking TenantContextError
rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach — a tenant DB read that catches and returns null/[]/a default re-masks a TenantContextError as a legitimate empty result (the 'data disappears' failure mode)
notes: Repo-wide sweep of the resolver-masking class into services (continuation of FARM-HIGH-080/085). 11 masking catch blocks across 7 files now re-throw TenantContextError at the top of the catch (import from @aquaculture/backend-common/database); the rest of each catch's behavior is preserved. Methods incl. growth-simulator.getTankBatch (was null), fcr-calculation.getTargetFCR (was 1.5 default), feed-consumption-forecast, daily-feeding-execution, regulatory-settings, sentinel-hub (per-tenant settings read), feeding-scheduler tenant-config reads. 37 OTHER catches were inspected and DELIBERATELY skipped (documented): Redis cache, external HTTP (marine-data/sentinel/mattilsynet/maskinporten), writes, rollback+rethrow, void event handlers, fail-closed readiness — none read tenant DB rows returning data, so there is nothing to mask. farm-service tsc 0; full farm handler/resolver/service/dataloader suite 818 green.

rule_violated: Farm Data SSOT plan section 3-D — an error-only view must not discard cached data on a refetch error (FARM-HIGH-064 class); gate the blocking view to initial-load failure only
notes: Completes the FARM-HIGH-064 (TanksPage) stale-on-error fix across farm-module. 13 pages/components gated their blocking error view behind isBlockingError(error, hasData) (the existing helper in utils/list-view-state.ts) so it fires ONLY on initial-load failure; on a refetch error with cached data they now keep rendering the data + show a non-blocking amber retry banner (mirroring TanksPage). hasData chosen per data shape (items?.length / array length / Boolean(data)). 6 components inspected and skipped as already-correct (error shown inline alongside data, or already guarded). farm-module tsc 0. Files: maintenance (Schedules/WorkOrders/SpareParts), health (HealthEvents), feeding (FeedingRecordsTab/PlannedVsActual/FeedingSummaryTab/DailyPlanTab/FeedInventoryTab/FeedingProgramForm), setup (SystemsTab), water-chemistry (ParameterConfigManager), cleaner-fish (TankCleanerFishCard).

title: guard_source_write trigger wrongly installed on cross-tenant farm.farm_audit_logs blocked every farm create/update audit-log write (P0999) so ALL /sites/setup mutations failed with a masked Bad Request

notes: Live-confirmed on prod: createSite died on the audit write. farm_audit_logs is source-only cross-tenant infra like outbox_events (correctly unguarded). Fixed by operator-approved live DROP TRIGGER + durable forward migration 1801600000000.

title: Farm /sites/setup write handlers wrote via pooled @InjectRepository to the source schema instead of the tenant schema (write-side mirror of the read-boundary gap)
rule_violated: Every tenant-scoped write must run through runInTenantTransaction + tenantManagerRepo so the INSERT lands in the tenant schema, not the source schema
notes: 43 of 92 farm command handlers lacked the boundary. This fix covers the 5 setup domains (create/update/delete) + worker update/delete + fish-health create. Remaining ~30 handlers tracked as ORPHAN-HIGH-251.

title: GraphQL defaultValue on tank create-DTO enum inputs breaks @nestjs/graphql enum key-to-value coercion so createTank was rejected at the ValidationPipe
rule_violated: Enum input fields must not carry a GraphQL defaultValue (it makes the raw uppercase key reach @IsEnum which validates the lowercase value); default in the handler instead
notes: tankType/material/waterType/status: defaultValue removed, made @IsOptional, defaults applied in CreateTankHandler. Same class in feeding/water-quality create-DTOs tracked as ORPHAN-HIGH-090b.

title: createHealthEvent rejected by a required @IsUUID on reportedBy (server-derived from the JWT) before the service could override it
rule_violated: Server-derived identity (reporter = JWT subject) must not be a required, format-constrained client input
notes: reportedBy made @IsOptional with the format constraint dropped; HealthEventService authoritatively sets it from user.sub. Service create also moved into the tenant write boundary.

title: createSpecies and createFeed enum inputs rejected at the ValidationPipe: species category/waterType carry a GraphQL defaultValue (missed by the .input.ts-only grep), and FeedType/FloatingType/FeedStatus were registered outside the entity so input enum coercion passed the raw uppercase key to @IsEnum
rule_violated: Enum input fields must not carry a GraphQL defaultValue, and registerEnumType must be co-located with the enum (in the entity the input imports) so input coercion maps the GraphQL key to the value before @IsEnum runs
notes: Follow-up to FARM-HIGH-090 found during live E2E after #756 deployed: 3 of 5 setup domains (consumable/supplier/chemical) + tanks worked; species + feed still failed. Species = same defaultValue class on category+waterType. Feed = FeedType registered only in feed.response.ts while create-feed.input.ts imports it from feed.entity.ts; co-located the registration in the entity (matching consumable/supplier/chemical). Other missed .dto.ts defaultValue files (batch, maintenance) tracked with ORPHAN-HIGH-090b.

title: equipmentList (ListEquipmentHandler) read equipment + tanks via raw injected repositories with no runInTenantRead boundary, causing intermittent silent-wrong-schema results (equipment appears then disappears)
rule_violated: Every tenant-scoped read must run through the fail-closed runInTenantRead boundary so it reads the tenant's own schema, not the ambient pooled-connection search_path
notes: Live-confirmed: 3 cage tanks correctly in tenant schema; only the READ flipped (N/0). Migrated both equipment + tanks query-builders to runInTenantRead + tenantManagerRepo (auto tenant scoping); equipment_types lookup routed through the boundary connection; removed from the read-boundary allowlist. Remaining auxiliary fail-open reads tracked ORPHAN-HIGH-094.

title: FarmSeedService reference-data seed transaction rolled back every boot because seedGlobalCleanerFishSpecies INSERTed without the NOT-NULL version column, leaving equipment_types/chemical_types/supplier_types empty in production (equipment create blocked)
rule_violated: A seed INSERT must populate all NOT-NULL columns; a failure in one reference seed must not silently roll back the entire reference-data transaction
notes: Root cause of 'cannot create equipment'. seedGlobalCleanerFishSpecies omitted version (@VersionColumn, NOT NULL, no default) -> rollback -> equipment_types/chemical_types/supplier_types all empty in prod. Fixed by version=1 in the seed. Existing tenant schemas need a post-deploy clone of reference rows from source (copyReferenceData is provisioning-time only).
